sources.entry: Unbury - Searches your saved browser bookmarks by meaning rather than by title, using a one-line description it writes for each link.

summary.one_liner: Unbury is a paid-API, arm64-only macOS app that searches your browser bookmarks by meaning, using a one-line description it writes for each saved link.
summary.what_it_does: It reads the bookmarks file from Brave, Chrome, Arc, Edge or Vivaldi, and generates a short description for each link. You search in plain language, and it ranks links by semantic similarity rather than matching words, so it can match across languages. Browsing by tags, filtering and all lists run locally on your Mac. "Ask Unbury" runs a conversation that performs its own searches, rephrases weak ones, and shows every search and link it read. A command-line tool, unburyctl, offers status, browsers, search, import, remove and restore commands. Deleting a link in Unbury does not delete it in the browser, and the app never writes to the browser's bookmarks.
use_cases: find a saved bookmark when you forget its title
search bookmarks in a different language than the page
browse and filter saved links by tag
ask questions across a collection of saved links
how_to_run: Open Unbury, then paste an OpenRouter or OpenAI API key in Settings
Press Import from browser and pick a profile
Alternatively, build from source: cd unbury/app && ./build.sh
stack: Claude Code, Codex, or OpenRouter models for descriptions
notable: Semantic search over bookmarks using AI-written descriptions
Import shows estimated cost before any spend
Ask Unbury shows every search and link it read
Local storage for links and vectors; only page text and queries go online
Signed, notarised, with built-in update feed
caveats: Searching requires a paid API key from OpenRouter or OpenAI; query embedding cannot run on the Mac
Supports only macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon; Intel builds are untested
Safari and Firefox bookmarks are not read yet
Personal project with no support promise and no roadmap
